tldr: Anthropic launched Claude for Small Business in late August with prebuilt connectors and ready-to-run workflows aimed at owners without technical staff. A nationwide SMB tour through September fed owner feedback straight back into the product.
whats_new: Anthropic shipped new Claude for Small Business workflows, integrations, and training programs on Sep 15 and kicked off the next leg of its SMB tour.
why_it_matters: It's a live case study in packaging agents for non-technical buyers: ship connectors instead of a raw API, then run a direct feedback loop before iterating.

status.detail: Anthropic is iterating on the small-business product in public, pairing each release with direct owner outreach.

beats.headline: Claude for Small Business ships with connectors and ready-run workflows
beats.summary: Initial package targets owners who lack technical staff to build their own integrations.

beats.headline: SMB tour surfaces what 1,000 owners actually need from AI
New workflows, integrations, and training land as the tour continues

open_questions: Which of the newly announced integrations ship first, and do they target the friction the tour surfaced?
Does the next SMB Tour leg publish adoption or retention numbers rather than anecdotes?
take_for_builders: Selling agent workflows to non-technical buyers: package prebuilt connectors instead of a raw API, and run a direct feedback loop with real customers before your next integration push.
